 orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order

1.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel with Ms. Suraiya Naaz, learned counsel for the petitioner 2.
Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. By the instant petition, the petitioner is praying for quashing of FIR dated 11.05.2025, bearing FIR No. 0144 of 2025 wherein the petitioner has been implicated for the offence punishable under Section 2/3 of the U.P. Gangster and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986.

entities.text: U.P. Gangster and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
4. It is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in the gang chart only one case has been shown which relates to Case Crime No. 164 of 2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420 read with Section 120B IPC registered at P.S. Raipur District Dehradun in which the offences have been compounded before the National Lok Adalat and, as such, the petitioner has been acquitted, therefore, the impugned FIR is liable to be quashed.

5. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner also submits that in the gang chart though there is reference of only one case but in a conclusion thereof there are reference of three cases, i.e.
Case Crime No. 496 of 2023, Case Crime of 2025 but there is no disclosure about the final outcome of these three cases, therefore, gang chart is in fact is not in conformity with Rule 5(3)(c) of U.P.
Gangster and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act.

entities.text:
U.P.
Gangster and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. On the previous date the State was directed to get instruction particularly about the three cases as above and now on instruction Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned A.G.A. apprise to this Court that in all these three cases charge sheet has been filed.

7. On this Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that gang chart has to be prepared with due deliberation of the official concerned but as it appears from the gang chart there is no deliberation with regard to the three other cases that is the reason in the chart there is WPCRL/547/2026 on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158295403/
1 reference of only one case in which the petitioner has already been acquitted by the National Lok Adalat after preparation of gang chart.
8. Primarily this Court is convinced with the submission of Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner that there is no due deliberation while preparing the gang chart.
8. Let the State may get instructions what would be the impact of three cases in which now charge sheet has been filed and furthermore what would be the impact of the order of National Lok Adalat whereby the offence relating to Case Crime NO. 164 of 2023 has been compounded.
Till the next date of listing, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner provided she cooperates with the investigation and will not indulge in any criminal activity in future.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 02.04.2026 Parul WPCRL/547/2026 on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158295403/
